arxiv-2304-10600.title: A Survey of Prevent and Detect Access Control Vulnerabilities
arxiv-2304-10600.creator: Li Zhong
arxiv-2304-10600.description: Abstract . Broken access control is one of the most common security vulnerabilities in web applications. These vulnerabilities are the major cause of many data breach incidents, which result in privacy concern and revenue loss. However, preventing and detecting access control vulnerabilities proactively in web applications could be difficult.

arxiv-2308-04403.title: Properties of sequence of linear functionals on B ​ V BV with applications
arxiv-2308-04403.creator: L-E. Persson, V. Tsagareishvili and G. Tutberidze
arxiv-2308-04403.description: Abstract . This paper is devoted to investigating the sequence of some linear functionals in the space B ​ V BV of finite variation functions. We prove that under certain conditions this sequence is bounded. We also prove that this result is sharp. In particular, the obtained results can be used to study convergence of some general Fourier series.

arxiv-2311-10831.title: Religious Competition, Culture and Domestic Violence: Evidence from Colombia
arxiv-2311-10831.creator: Hector Galindo-Silva, Guy Tchuente
arxiv-2311-10831.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hector Galindo-Silva, Guy Tchuente. This paper studies how religious competition, as measured by the emergence of religious organizations with innovative worship styles and cultural practices, impacts domestic violence. Using data from Colombia, the study estimates a two-way fixed-effects model and reveals that the establishment of the first non-Catholic church in a predominantly Catholic municipality leads to a significant decrease in reported cases of domestic violence.

arxiv-2312-01001.title: Learning county from pixels: Corn yield prediction with attention-weighted multiple instance learning
arxiv-2312-01001.creator: Xiaoyu Wang a , Yuchi Ma b , Yijia Xu a , Qunying Huang c , Zhengwei Yang d , Zhou Zhang a
arxiv-2312-01001.description: Abstract Remote sensing has become a promising tool in yield prediction. Most prior work using satellite imagery for county-level corn yield prediction spatially aggregates all pixels within a county into a single value, potentially overlooking the detailed information and valuable insights offered by more granular data.

arxiv-2312-02710.title: User Interaction Data in Apps: Comparing Policy Claims to Implementations Thanks: Published at the 18th IFIP Summer School on Privacy and Identity Management 2023 (IFIPSC 2023). Affiliation: Norwegian Computing Center
arxiv-2312-02710.creator: Feiyang Tang, Bjarte M. Østvold
arxiv-2312-02710.description: Abstract As mobile app usage continues to rise, so does the generation of extensive user interaction data, which includes actions such as swiping, zooming, or the time spent on a screen. Apps often collect a large amount of this data and claim to anonymize it, yet concerns arise regarding the adequacy of these measures.

arxiv-2402-09496.creator: Ivan Chajda, Helmut Länger
arxiv-2402-09496.description: Abstract Tolerance relations were investigated by several authors in various algebraic structures, see e.g. the monograph [ 2 ] . Recently G. Czédli [ 6 ] studied so-called 2 2 -uniform tolerances on lattices, i.e. tolerances that are compatible with the lattice operations and whose blocks are of cardinality 2 2 .

arxiv-2407-14622.title: BOND : Aligning LLMs with Best-of- N Distillation
arxiv-2407-14622.creator: Pier Giuseppe Sessa, Robert Dadashi, Léonard Hussenot, Johan Ferret, Nino Vieillard, Alexandre Ramé, Bobak Shariari, Sarah Perrin, Abe Friesen, Geoffrey Cideron, Sertan Girgin, Piotr Stanczyk, Andrea Michi, Danila Sinopalnikov, Sabela Ramos, Amélie Héliou, Aliaksei Severyn, Matt Hoffman, Nikola Momc
arxiv-2407-14622.description: Abstract Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) is a key driver of quality and safety in state-of-the-art large language models. Yet, a surprisingly simple and strong inference-time strategy is Best-of- N sampling that selects the best generation among N N candidates.

arxiv-2409-07905.title: Supernova remnants in clumpy medium: A model of hydrodynamic and radio synchrotron evolution
arxiv-2409-07905.creator: Petar Kostić, Bojan Arbutina, Branislav Vukotić, Dejan Urošević
arxiv-2409-07905.description: Abstract We present an analytical model of Σ \Sigma – D D relation for supernova remnants (SNRs) evolving in a clumpy medium. The model and its approximations were developed using the hydrodynamic simulations of SNRs in environments of low-density bubbles and clumpy media with different densities and volume-filling factors.

arxiv-2506-00199.title: A chip-scale atomic beam source for non-classical light
arxiv-2506-00199.creator: Braden J. Larsen, Hagan Hensley, Gabriela D. Martinez, Alexander Staron, William R. McGehee, John Kitching, James K. Thompson
arxiv-2506-00199.description: Abstract Room temperature thermal atoms have proven to be a powerful resource for magnetometry, electrometry, atom-entanglement generation, and robust atomic clocks. Recent efforts have sought to realize compact and highly manufacturable atomic vapors and atomic beams for chip-scale magnetometry and atomic clocks.

Photometric redshifts (photo- z z ’s) are crucial for the cosmology, galaxy evolution, and transient science drivers of next-generation imaging facilities like the Euclid Mission, the Rubin Observatory, and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Previous work has shown that image-based deep learning photo- z z methods produce smaller scatter than photometry-based classical machine learning (ML) methods on the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Main Galaxy Sample, a testbed photo- z z dataset.

This paper reports a 5.96 Gbp genome assembly of grasspea genotype LS007, of which 5.

pmc-12801070.title: Hybrid Tie-Grip Suture Repair for Isolated Radial Tears in the Middle Segment of the Lateral Meniscus
pmc-12801070.creator: Ryohei Uchida, Shuji Horibe, Tomoki Ohori, Toshitaka Tsunematu, Hiroyuki Tanaka, Seiji Okada, Ryo Iuchi
pmc-12801070.description: Radial tears in the middle segment are the most common type of traumatic lateral meniscus injury in young athletes with stable knees. Conventionally, meniscectomy was the first-line treatment for this type of tear, but it did not prevent degenerative changes or decreases in meniscal function.

pmc-12804914.title: Research on ambidextrous digital innovation strategies of SMEs embedded in industrial internet platforms based on evolutionary game theory
pmc-12804914.creator: CaiYun Zhuang, Yu Lin, LiLi Wang
pmc-12804914.description: In the accelerating digital economy, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) encounter a dual challenge in pursuing ambidextrous digital innovation (exploratory and exploitative), constrained by limited resources and path dependence. Industrial internet platforms, functioning as central hubs for resources, technologies, and data, play a pivotal role in addressing these challenges.

pmc-12939315.title: Indium phosphide quantum dots: advanced synthesis, surface engineering, and biomedical applications in imaging, sensing, and therapy
pmc-12939315.creator: A. K. Kareem, Musallam Ahmed Salim Tabook, Esraa H. J. Mahdi, Ahmed Said Badawy, M. M. Rekha, Laxmidhar Maharana, P. Grace Kanmani Prince, Gaganjot Kaur, Hamza Fadhel Hamzah, Nadia Sarhan
pmc-12939315.description: Indium phosphide quantum dots (InP QDs) are emerging as non-toxic, tunable, and biocompatible semiconductor nanomaterials with transformative potential in biomedical applications. This review highlights cutting-edge synthesis methods, including nonclassical nucleation and scalable production, alongside innovative surface engineering techniques such as ligand exchange, polymer coatings, and inorganic passivation to overcome challenges like surface defects and indium release.

pmc-12986692.title: Culinary Nutrition Programming for Members of a Community-Based Cancer Program
pmc-12986692.creator: Billie Jane C. Hermosura, Meaghan E. Kavanagh, Jaime Slavin, David J. A. Jenkins, Amy Symington
pmc-12986692.description: (1) Background: Nutrition research in cancer care has largely focused on disease prevention and management, overlooking the importance of food literacy. Culinary cancer care programs may address this gap by facilitating the practical application of nutrition through culinary skills, fostering social connections over nutrient-dense meals, and supporting individuals during periods of physical and social vulnerability.

pmc-13091298.title: Fluorescently engineered KRAS-mutant organoids as versatile tools for in vitro and in vivo cancer modeling
pmc-13091298.creator: Alireza Savadipour, Krishna S. Tummala, Eric S. Muise, Mark Buchanan, Vania Vidimar, Mike Veling, Jun Liu, Johnny Kopinja, Charlie Schneider, Brian Pak Ho Chan, Richard Carr, Scott Norton, John M. Gaspar, Jennifer Piesvaux, Erica Leccese, Eunsil Park, Lily Y. Moy, Brian J. Long, Nicolas Solban
pmc-13091298.description: Organoids have emerged as advanced models in cancer research, offering superior physiological relevance compared to traditional 2D cell cultures. They mimic the three-dimensional architecture and tumor clonal heterogeneity, providing more accurate insights into tumor biology and drug responses.Despite these advantages, organoid-based studies pose significant technical challenges. In in-vitro studies, imaging and drug screening—particularly in co-culture systems—can be difficult.

pmc-13527494.title: Neurocognitive Mechanisms of Preventive Cognitive Therapy as Relapse Prevention in Remitted Major Depressive Disorder: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-13527494.creator: Marie-José van Tol, Rozemarijn van Kleef, Ronja Eike, Evelien van Valen, Jan-Bernard Marsman, Remco Renken, André Aleman, Claudi Bockting
pmc-13527494.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMajor depressive disorder (MDD) is a highly recurrent psychiatric disorder. Understanding mechanisms of effective treatments that lower recurrence risk provides an opportunity to identify neurocognitive targets for recurrence prevention. Here we studied neurocognitive mechanisms of preventive cognitive therapy (PCT).MethodsFifty medication-free individuals who were remitted from MDD and at high risk for recurrence were randomized to 8 sessions of protocolized PCT or a waiting list control (WLC) group as part of the NEWPRIDE (Neurocognitive Working Mechanisms of the Prevention of Relapse in Depression)

pmc-13677634.title: Validation of 3D intraoral scanner use for detecting caries lesions around dental restorations: A diagnostic accuracy study
pmc-13677634.creator: Bruna Machado Fernandes, Anelise Fernandes Montagner, Sarah Arangurem Karam, Françoise Helene van de Sande, Marcos Britto Correa
pmc-13677634.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesThis study aimed to validate the use of a 3D intraoral scanner (IOS) for detecting secondary caries lesions around restorations using image-based CARS-derived severity categories, compared with visual-tactile clinical examination.Materials and methodsA diagnostic validation study was conducted at the university clinical facilities, from July 2023 to September 2024, including adult patients with amalgam or composite resin restorations on anterior and posterior teeth. The restorations were assessed using visual-tactile clinical examination, adopted as the clinical reference standard, and IOS image-based assessment.
